utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Good morning, Your Honours. Good morning to everybody in and around the courtroom. This is case IT-08-91-T, the Prosecutor versus Mico Stanisic and Stojan Zupljanin.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Registrar. Good morning to everyone. May we have the appearances, please.

utterances.speaker: MS. PIDWELL
utterances.text: Good morning, Your Honours. Tom Hannis, Belinda Pidwell, and Crispian Smith for the Prosecution.

utterances.speaker: MR. CVIJETIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good morning, Your Honours. Mr. Stanisic's Defence comprises of Slobodan Cvijetic, Tatjana Savic, Ms. Deirdre Montgomery.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: Good morning, Your Honours. Dragan Krgovic, Igor Pantelic, and Aleksandar Aleksic for Zupljanin Defence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: Thank you. Before we call the witness to continue his testimony, the Trial Chamber notes that the first witness subject to the Prosecution's 15th motion for protective measures filed on the 20th of September is scheduled to appear on Friday, the 8th of October. That's today week. The Defence is hereby instructed to file their response by Tuesday, the 5th of October. Thank you. And if there's nothing else, could the witness be escorted back to the stand, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: Mr. Miskovic, good morning to you, sir. Before Ms. Pidwell continues, I remind you you're still on your oath.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: Yes, Ms. Pidwell.

utterances.speaker: MS. PIDWELL
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MS. PIDWELL
utterances.text: Good morning, sir.

utterances.speaker: SIMO MISKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Good morning.

utterances.speaker: MS. PIDWELL
utterances.text: Yesterday you were telling us about the Prijedor 2 police station. And if you can please tell us now where that station is actually located in Prijedor.

utterances.speaker: SIMO MISKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The police station was in the local community office, Prijedor Dva. It was there ever since it was established. That was the seat, and that was the place where everybody gathered.

utterances.speaker: MS. PIDWELL
utterances.text: Is that in Prijedor town itself?

utterances.speaker: SIMO MISKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. That is the outskirts of Prijedor, a suburb of Prijedor, but now it's all become one.

utterances.speaker: MS. PIDWELL
utterances.text: Are you familiar with the Keraterm factory in Prijedor?

utterances.speaker: SIMO MISKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It was also in the area of the Prijedor 2 local commune on the Prijedor-Banja Luka road.

utterances.speaker: MS. PIDWELL
utterances.text: So how far from the Keraterm factory was this located?

utterances.speaker: SIMO MISKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Perhaps 2 or 2 and a half kilometres. 2 kilometres, as the crow flies. About 2 kilometres.

utterances.speaker: MS. PIDWELL
utterances.text: Thank you. Now, we heard yesterday that your wartime assignment was to become the commander of the Prijedor 2 station. About how many police officers were under your command in that role?

utterances.speaker: SIMO MISKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I've already forgotten. But I think not more than 100. Up to 100. Between 80 and 100, approximately.

utterances.speaker: MS. PIDWELL
utterances.text: And when you worked at the Prijedor main station before your retirement, how many active police officers worked based out of that station?

utterances.speaker: SIMO MISKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: About the same number, as far as I can remember. It was quite a while ago. 20 years ago, or more.

utterances.speaker: MS. PIDWELL
utterances.text: And when you held the post of commander of the Prijedor 2 station, who did you report to?

utterances.speaker: SIMO MISKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Along the line of reporting, the police station commanders would report to the chiefs of the SUP. So yesterday when we talked about the stations, I said that there was the centre and the Ljubija police station. And then the substations were Omarska and Kozarac. So they were directly connected to the MUP chief, the stations, and the substations were reporting to the stations and the patrol sectors that the station used to cover certain areas, specific areas.

utterances.speaker: MS. PIDWELL
utterances.text: And when you say that you were -- you reported to the chief of the SUP, who was that in 1991 in Prijedor?

utterances.speaker: SIMO MISKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: In 1991, I was retired.

utterances.speaker: MS. PIDWELL
utterances.text: I'm referring to the period of time, sir, when you held the position of commander of the Prijedor 2 station.

utterances.speaker: SIMO MISKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Oh, when it was activated, that was our wartime assignment in the reserve Prijedor 2 station when the station was activated in the second half of 1992, then everybody reported, including myself as the commander of the station, and the station as the station was reporting to the chief of the Prijedor MUP. That's how the organisation was anyway.

utterances.speaker: MS. PIDWELL
utterances.text: Yes. If we go back, sir, it's been recorded that the Prijedor 2 station was activated in the second half of 1992. Was that recorded correctly?

utterances.speaker: SIMO MISKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. The second half, yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. PIDWELL
utterances.text: But, sir, your -- the position that you took at the Prijedor 2 station was in 1991, was it not?

utterances.speaker: SIMO MISKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I -- I explained already. The reserve police stations were formed in the early 1970s, as far as I can remember, and their main function was to prepare a certain number of cadres for possible war circumstances and these were mostly people working on completely different jobs in different organisations, so it was a regular thing to have training from the 1970s, lectures, shooting target practice. All these things were done by these members of the reserve police forces since that time.

utterances.speaker: MS. PIDWELL
utterances.text: Sir, you were not -- did you not hold the position of police commander of the Prijedor 2 police station in 1992, did you?

utterances.speaker: SIMO MISKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That is correct, no, I did not. The commander of the reserve police station, Prijedor 2, was something that I did for two months, because then I became the president of the Serbian Democratic Party in Prijedor and I was not able to perform both functions, both the political and the police duty, so there was a suggestion and an agreement was reached for someone else to take the post of the commander of the Prijedor 2 police station, and that I should withdraw from that post and that's what happened. So Knezevic, Zivko succeeded me in that post. Up until that time he was one of the deputy police commanders in Prijedor.

utterances.speaker: MS. PIDWELL
utterances.text: Thank you. And what was his nationality -- ethnicity?

utterances.speaker: SIMO MISKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Zivko was a Serb.

utterances.speaker: MS. PIDWELL
utterances.text: And was he a career policeman, or was he a political appointment?

utterances.speaker: SIMO MISKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: He was a professional policeman. He was deputy police commander and he also -- was already retired. He retired before I, did but he also had his wartime assignment but it was not in the area of Prijedor 2. That was me. I don't know where he was assigned but after I withdrew, he came and succeeded me in that particular post.

utterances.speaker: MS. PIDWELL
utterances.text: If we just go back a little way, sir, if we can clarify when you held this post as the commander of Prijedor 2, who was the chief of the Prijedor SJB at that time?

utterances.speaker: SIMO MISKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: At the time the party elections were held, there was a change of the leadership cadre structure and some institutions, including the MUP in Prijedor, it was headed by Telundzic. This was pursuant to the agreement among parties. Earlier you saw that later there was some problems about the division of power between the parties in Prijedor and this later escalated to certain aggravated situations.

utterances.speaker: MS. PIDWELL
utterances.text: What was the ethnicity of Mr. Telundzic?

utterances.speaker: SIMO MISKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: He was a Muslim. I apologise, I'm using the term "Muslim" throughout this time because, at that time, that was the term that was used. I don't know if there are problems or not with me using that term, but I would like to be quite clear about that.

utterances.speaker: MS. PIDWELL
utterances.text: Thank you. In 1991, did you know Simo Drljaca?

utterances.speaker: SIMO MISKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It just happened that I know Simo Drljaca from boyhood. His father, Pero, was a police commander throughout that whole time, after World War II this was how he was appointed by decree. Actually, that was my father. His father, Veljko, was a policeman under my father, so it just happened in these circumstances that we knew each other. But we didn't really meet or see each other or socialise after that boyhood period. He worked in the social community for high school education and he was in the education profession. He was a -- dealing with teachers, professors. That was his profession.

utterances.speaker: MS. PIDWELL
utterances.text: And it's correct, sir, isn't it, that he lived not far from you in the town of Prijedor?

utterances.speaker: SIMO MISKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: He lived in the centre of town. I lived in Urije. We -- I have a family house there. My father had a house there, and I built myself a house behind it. So whether it was close or -- or far, it's a relative thing. He lived in the centre of town, and I lived in Prijedor Dva. It's about 2 kilometres from the centre.

utterances.speaker: MS. PIDWELL
utterances.text: In 1991, what position did Simo Drljaca hold?

utterances.speaker: SIMO MISKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: In 1991, Simo was the secretary of the self-interest community for high school education.

utterances.speaker: MS. PIDWELL
utterances.text: During the -- during the two months that you held the position of commander of the Prijedor 2 station, what -- what -- what was your obligation to report matters to the chief of the -- the SUP?

utterances.speaker: SIMO MISKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Nothing particular. Regular daily activities, everything that is part of police work, anything that is recorded out in the field. This would be reported to me by the policemen, and then I would report back to the chief. And it -- this also applied if there were any kind of problems that happened.

utterances.speaker: MS. PIDWELL
utterances.text: And what form did the reporting take?

utterances.speaker: SIMO MISKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, mostly often this was at the collegium meetings where the commanders of the police and other cadres were called. For example, you had the inner collegium and the broader collegium in Prijedor. The inner collegium was the top leadership, and the broader collegium consisted of lower-ranking leaders in the Prijedor MUP.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: Why this is relevant? It's 1991. It is out of scope of the indictment.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: Ms. Pidwell.

utterances.speaker: MS. PIDWELL
utterances.text: It's background information, sir. This police station was operational during the indictment period, and it's the Prosecution's case that this is relevant to what happened a few months later in this municipality.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: Yes. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MS. PIDWELL
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. PIDWELL
utterances.text: Now, sir, were you involved in the -- in the multi-party elections that took place at the end of 1990?

utterances.speaker: SIMO MISKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. PIDWELL
utterances.text: And --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Interpreter did not understand what the witness said.

utterances.speaker: MS. PIDWELL
utterances.text: Sorry --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: The witness -- Mr. Witness, could you please repeat your answer. The interpreters didn't get it. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I did take part in the elections in 1991, as a citizen.

utterances.speaker: MS. PIDWELL
utterances.text: And please correct me if I'm wrong, but there were 90 seats.

utterances.speaker: SIMO MISKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: 1990 or 1991. The elections were either in 1990 or 1991. I don't recall exactly whether it was 1990 or 1991. The multi-party election.

utterances.speaker: MS. PIDWELL
utterances.text: Sir, please correct me if I'm wrong, but there were 90 seats in the Municipal Assembly of Prijedor; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: SIMO MISKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't recall that. I wasn't directly involved in the work of the electoral commission. I took part in the elections as a citizen.

utterances.speaker: MS. PIDWELL
utterances.text: Are you aware that after the elections the key positions in Prijedor were distributed according to party positions?

utterances.speaker: SIMO MISKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: This was done in the municipality. This was an agreement that was not of something that we had any influence on. They agreed and took certain posts on the basis of results of the multi-party elections. And the citizens, we were informed about that, who took which post, who was the president, who was the secretary, the vice-president, the president of the Executive Board. That is when we were informed about it as citizens. But these were talks that were conducted within and among the political parties, and as citizens, we didn't know about it until they informed us about the situation. We didn't know how this was done.

utterances.speaker: MS. PIDWELL
utterances.text: I have just received a message, a request from the interpreters that if possible, you could slow down so they could catch what you are saying.

utterances.speaker: SIMO MISKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No problem. One speaks in the usual way that I'm used to, but I will just try to pause a little bit.

utterances.speaker: MS. PIDWELL
utterances.text: Thank you. Now after these elections, some commissions were set up by the individual parties to try and negotiate those positions that couldn't be agreed upon. Do you recall that?

utterances.speaker: SIMO MISKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's what I find as a situation which means that the commissions had existed before but they couldn't agree on anything. When I became party head, that was one of the crucial problems that could -- could have generated a crisis in the area. And as the head of the party, I wanted to have proper information, and that's why I placed myself as the leader of that commission that was supposed to negotiate with the other parties. And let me just finish this. Our first talks with the representatives of the SDA in -- on the premises of the tax authorities were one of the representatives of the SDA and the member of their commission was also an official of the tax administration was successful. There was a lot of goodwill and we managed to distribute positions amongst ourselves within the first half an hour. And we agreed that on the following day, we would continue distributing the other 50 percent of the functions and positions, but that meeting, on the following day, actually never materialised.

utterances.speaker: MS. PIDWELL
utterances.text: And just to clarify, sir, which party were you representing?

utterances.speaker: SIMO MISKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Of the Serbian Democratic Party, because I was also its president. And there was a lot of goodwill on both sides, in both commissions, and within the first two hours we managed to distribute 50 per cent of the functions. We were supposed to continue the following day, however, the SDA commission was blocked by their political leadership. Therefore, the talks never continued after that.

utterances.speaker: MS. PIDWELL
utterances.text: Were you a member of this commission before you became the party president in September?

utterances.speaker: SIMO MISKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I did not know that it existed. I was not involved. Only when I became party leader I learnt about that. And in order to gain proper information, I put myself at the head of the commission and our first task was to distribute functions and positions in the territory of the municipality of Prijedor.

utterances.speaker: MS. PIDWELL
utterances.text: Right. Let's have a look at some those functions and positions. What position was held by Muhamed Cehajic in 1991 when you became party leader?

utterances.speaker: SIMO MISKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Cehajic. Muhamed Cehajic was president of the Municipal Assembly of Prijedor, according to the party results that ensued as a distribution of political positions in the authorities, in the government.

utterances.speaker: MS. PIDWELL
utterances.text: And which party was he a member of?

utterances.speaker: SIMO MISKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The SDA.

utterances.speaker: MS. PIDWELL
utterances.text: What about Milomir Stakic?

utterances.speaker: SIMO MISKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Milomir Stakic was vice-president of that same Assembly, Cehajic's vice-president.

utterances.speaker: MS. PIDWELL
utterances.text: And which party was he a member of?

utterances.speaker: SIMO MISKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The SDS.

utterances.speaker: MS. PIDWELL
utterances.text: What about Milan Kovacevic?

utterances.speaker: SIMO MISKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Milan Kovacevic was the president of the executive board, the president of the executive power on behalf of the SDS, the Serbian Democratic Party.

utterances.speaker: MS. PIDWELL
utterances.text: Do you recall Dusan Baltic?

utterances.speaker: SIMO MISKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Baltic. Yes, I do remember him. He was the secretary of the assembly. He was a lawyer by profession. He a degree in law.

utterances.speaker: MS. PIDWELL
utterances.text: Which party was he a member of?

utterances.speaker: SIMO MISKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know if he was a member of any party, but if he was, then he was a member of the Serbian Democratic Party.

utterances.speaker: MS. PIDWELL
utterances.text: What was his ethnicity?

utterances.speaker: SIMO MISKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Serb.

utterances.speaker: MS. PIDWELL
utterances.text: Let's turn now to Milorad Milakovic?

utterances.speaker: SIMO MISKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Milakovic? He was nothing. Did he not hold any positions either in the police -- or, rather, he was the first president of the Serbian Democratic Party, and then he was replaced by Srdjo and then there were problems, I don't now what problems, and then I followed as the third in that sequence.

utterances.speaker: MS. PIDWELL
utterances.text: When you say Srdjo, do you mean Srdjo Srdic?

utterances.speaker: SIMO MISKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Srdjo Srdic, yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. PIDWELL
utterances.text: Can you tell us who Radomir Neskovic was and his position?

utterances.speaker: SIMO MISKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Radomir Neskovic was a member of the Main Board of the Serbian Democratic Party of Bosnia and Herzegovina; later on, Republika Srpska.

utterances.speaker: MS. PIDWELL
utterances.text: And Colonel Arsic?

utterances.speaker: SIMO MISKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Colonel Arsic was an active JNA officer, and he was deployed in Prijedor.

utterances.speaker: MS. PIDWELL
utterances.text: What was his ethnicity?

utterances.speaker: SIMO MISKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Serb. And he also hailed from Serbia. He was not a native of our area.

utterances.speaker: MS. PIDWELL
utterances.text: Who was Dragan Savanovic?

utterances.speaker: SIMO MISKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Dragan Savanovic was a member of the Serbian Democratic Party from day one. He became a member even before me. He participated in the multi-party elections and he was a deputy in the municipality. And there were Serbs in other parties who also participated in the work of the Assembly but he was also the president of the group of Serbian representatives in the Municipal Assembly of Prijedor.

utterances.speaker: MS. PIDWELL
utterances.text: Thank you. Mirza Mujadzic. Sir, who was Mirza Mujadzic?

utterances.speaker: SIMO MISKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Mirza Mujadzic was a physician in the health centre in Prijedor, and after the multi-party elections, he was elected as the president of the SDA, the Party of Democratic Action of the Municipal Board of Prijedor.

utterances.speaker: MS. PIDWELL
utterances.text: And, finally, if you could tell us who Slobodan Kuruzovic was?

utterances.speaker: SIMO MISKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Slobodan Kuruzovic was a teacher in one of the primary schools. I don't know in which one. And his war assignment was to be the commander of the TO. He was a reserve major. That's the rank that he held.

utterances.speaker: MS. PIDWELL
utterances.text: What was his ethnicity?

utterances.speaker: SIMO MISKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Serb.

utterances.speaker: MS. PIDWELL
utterances.text: Now, sir, we know that you became the president of the SDS party in September of 1991. I want you now to have a look at a document. It's 65 ter 10284/50.

utterances.speaker: MS. PIDWELL
utterances.text: While that's coming up on the screen, sir, over the last couple of days, do you recall listening to the audiotape of two intercepts, two telephone conversations?

utterances.speaker: SIMO MISKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I apologise. Repeat your question.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, once again I would have to object to this line of questioning. Again we're in 1991. The intercept between Radovan Karadzic and other participants, why is that relevant for this case? Why are we dealing with 1991 and we're not dealing with anything that is relevant for this indictment and for this trial.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: 1991 intercept, Ms. Pidwell?

utterances.speaker: MS. PIDWELL
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour. It's an intercept between this gentleman, two others and Radovan Karadzic. Your Honours are aware that JCE forms a large part of our indictment, and it shows the relationship between the two, the arrangement that were put in place by the SDS in 1991 or the events that took place in 1992, and in my submission it is fully relevant. It is already an exhibit, Your Honour, and this man was involved in the conversation.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: I see.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, but what has it got to do with this indictment and with the police and with this trial? This is not the Karadzic trial, is it?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: Mr. Krgovic, isn't it the rule of evidence that -- and procedure, that, whereas, an indictment has to be drawn with a certain measure of precision in order to make a trial manageable, the events which -- out of the context of which that indictment or the allegations come, doesn't exist in isolation and therefore it is permissible as a matter of evidence to set the context in which the relevant charge is laid. Isn't that the well-settled rule, Mr. Krgovic? Please proceed, Ms. Pidwell.

utterances.speaker: MS. PIDWELL
utterances.text: Thank you, sir.

utterances.speaker: MS. PIDWELL
utterances.text: Sir -- do you recall listening to an audio version of this intercept a couple of days ago?

utterances.speaker: SIMO MISKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I have to inform the Trial Chamber about that conversation. During that conversation, I was not the president of the SDS. They had approached me four or five times with a proposal but I refused. I didn't want them to deal with my name. I didn't know the people that I was supposed to work with. On the fourth or fifth occasion, they managed to convince me to join the party. I felt at that time that it was my obligation to help as much as I could. They thought that I met all the requirements, that's how I accepted, and within that context there was a conversation between Srdjo Srdic who was the president of the party at that time, myself, the representative of the Main Board, Mr. Neskovic, and Radovan Karadzic as the president of the party.

utterances.speaker: MS. PIDWELL
utterances.text: Thank you, sir. And just on that, when you say "they approached me," who do you mean?

utterances.speaker: SIMO MISKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, a commission, a delegation on behalf of the SDS, Savanovic, Milomir Stakic. I can't remember them all. A few of them, in any case, were members of that delegation. They had problems and they thought that I might be able to deal with all the problems in the party, and I accepted eventually and that's when the conversation took place. I was still not the president of the party. Srdjo Srdic was the president of the party. He participated in the conversation, I did as well. Neskovic was a member of the Main Board who was in charge of dealing with the situation in the party in Prijedor and the president of the party, Radovan Karadzic.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Could the witness please be asked to slow down and articulate. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: Mr. Miskovic, again, the interpreters are asking you to pace yourself so that they can -- I can empathise with you. I have the same problem.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] It is very difficult to control what I want to say, my conversation, and the obligation towards others. That's a very difficult thing to do.

utterances.speaker: MS. PIDWELL
utterances.text: Sir, do you recall listening to this conversation on an audio cassette in the last couple of days?

utterances.speaker: SIMO MISKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, the complete conversation reflect what the conversation was all about at the time.

utterances.speaker: MS. PIDWELL
utterances.text: Did you recognise your own voice?

utterances.speaker: SIMO MISKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. I also recognised the context of the conversation. When I listened to it, I remember the context of the conversation.

utterances.speaker: MS. PIDWELL
utterances.text: Where was this call made from?

utterances.speaker: SIMO MISKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: From Srdjo's apartment. From Srdjo Srdic's apartment.

utterances.speaker: MS. PIDWELL
utterances.text: And you've referred to the context and given us a little bit of information about that. But can you summarise for us why this conversation was made to Dr. Karadzic at this time?

utterances.speaker: SIMO MISKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The conversation took place because there had been problems in the party. Neskovic explained that. There were two streams in the party. I didn't know all that. But I suppose that had been the reason why they asked me to join the party because they thought I would be able to deal with all that. There were confrontations between two streams or two different parties within the party. One was led by Srdjo Srdic, followed by some older cadre in the party, and the others were all younger, and young people wanted quicker changes and they probably felt animosity toward the older -- the older -- the old being old wanted to control everything in the party and that was the conversation. And that's why things had to be unified in order to prevent the breakup of the party and modalities had to be found as to how to deal with the situation and how to secure all that, to secure the smooth functioning of the party and not its division. And from the context of this conversation, can you see that President Karadzic said if they want to do so, they can establish their own party. They can't be on the list on the SDS and use that to further their own goals. From that, I can see that there was a confrontation between the two groups, and I don't know who was right and who was wrong.

utterances.speaker: MS. PIDWELL
utterances.text: If we can turn to the page 3 on the English, please. I think it's the same page in the B/C/S. It's -- sorry. The B/C/S is the preceding page, 3006. Yes, thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. PIDWELL
utterances.text: Sir, this is the portion of the conversation between Dr. Karadzic and Neskovic. And if you --

utterances.speaker: SIMO MISKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. PIDWELL
utterances.text: And Neskovic is saying that: "They do not recognise any authority here, especially if you mention Sarajevo." Can you see that portion?

utterances.speaker: SIMO MISKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. PIDWELL
utterances.text: And Karadzic then continues and says: "Whoever refuses to obey Sarajevo should resign. Write papers for them tomorrow and say this is a party which has its top and its bottom and nobody will fuck under our name, fuck about under our name."

utterances.speaker: SIMO MISKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. PIDWELL
utterances.text: What do you think he meant by that?

utterances.speaker: SIMO MISKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I really don't know. You have to ask him. As a layman I would say that he's talking about the party policies and that everybody has to subscribe to those. Either you fall in or you leave, and that's the case all over the world. You can't be against the party and be a member of it.

utterances.speaker: MS. PIDWELL
utterances.text: If we now go to the next page in the English, page 4. The next page in the B/C/S.

utterances.speaker: MS. PIDWELL
utterances.text: This is a portion where you see you come onto the line. And Karadzic says: "Put Miskovic on, please." Did you know Dr. Karadzic at this time?

utterances.speaker: SIMO MISKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. I knew him from the press. I knew all of them after the pre-election campaigns and the activities that they were involved in.

utterances.speaker: MS. PIDWELL
utterances.text: So this was the first time you'd actually spoken to him?

utterances.speaker: SIMO MISKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, yes, yes, the first time.

utterances.speaker: MS. PIDWELL
utterances.text: And he -- sorry. You start talking about the Main Board. Which Main Board are you talking about when you say: "I'm not a member of the Main Board?"

utterances.speaker: SIMO MISKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The Main Board of the Serbian Democratic Party in Prijedor, or, rather, not the Main Board but the Municipal Board. I said the Main Board because I was not aware of the organisation that was in place. I had just joined. So this referred to the Municipal Board most probably I had been informed in the meantime that the president is elected from the Municipal Board and that's why I perhaps said that I was not a member of the Municipal Board but the Main Board and it was my mistake that -- I misspoke and that's the context in which the words were used.

utterances.speaker: MS. PIDWELL
utterances.text: And when Dr. Karadzic says: "They cannot give them carte blanche. They are implementing the policies of the party, not the other way around." What was he referring to?

utterances.speaker: SIMO MISKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I was there, and he said that they should further the party policies not some other policies. If they wanted to pursue other policies they had to change their party membership and that's typical of all parties in the world. Those who don't like the party they're with, change things. They establish new parties.

utterances.speaker: MS. PIDWELL
utterances.text: If we go now, please, to page 12 of the English transcript. And in the B/C/S, it's the page headed 3013.

utterances.speaker: MS. PIDWELL
utterances.text: This is the portion of the conversation, sir, when Dr. Karadzic is once again talking to Srdja. That's Srdjo Srdic.

utterances.speaker: SIMO MISKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. PIDWELL
utterances.text: And he says, Karadzic says: "Srdja, you see it is not working. The party is stuck. It is not working. You have to yield and let someone finish it." Do you see that portion?

utterances.speaker: SIMO MISKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I do. Yes, I do.

utterances.speaker: MS. PIDWELL
utterances.text: And did Srdja Srdic yield?

utterances.speaker: SIMO MISKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know what they meant. I was listening to this and I did not hear the conversation or, rather, the words of President Karadzic, but I heard what Srdjo Srdic was saying because I was there. I don't know what the yielding was all about, and I know that eventually I was elected the president of the party and that Srdja also remained in the party and that the dissidents, as it were, also remained in the party so I really don't know within that -- within what context was this word used, what was the meaning the word, when he said yielded. And he must have yielded since he accepted me as the president of the party. Did he not object. He did not put up any resistance together with the group of the members of the party that supported him, that was case.

utterances.speaker: MS. PIDWELL
utterances.text: And you became the president of the SDS party the very next day, did you not?

utterances.speaker: SIMO MISKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: 11 September 1991. I was elected at an assembly meeting -- or, rather, that was the party assembly which held place in the Prijedor theatre.

utterances.speaker: MS. PIDWELL
utterances.text: And after you took over as the role of the president, did you have regular meetings?

utterances.speaker: SIMO MISKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, my principle was to hold regular meetings, to inform each other, to keep abreast of the problems, to find solutions to certain problems, to find people who will be dealing with problems. I thought that was the best type of communication for anybody who wanted to do things right. That was my principle that I adhered to.

utterances.speaker: MS. PIDWELL
utterances.text: How often, on average, would these meetings take place?

utterances.speaker: SIMO MISKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Once a week. Once in seven days. I believe that we even had a regular slot on Thursdays, as far as I can remember.

utterances.speaker: MS. PIDWELL
utterances.text: Were minutes taken of these meetings?

utterances.speaker: SIMO MISKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, handwritten minutes. Before me there were no minutes. No minutes were taken of any of the meetings, so I was forced to give a task to the secretary to write notes, to write the minutes. I replaced the secretary that I found when I joined and I brought in a new person who was very professional and who kept the minutes of all of the sessions of the Municipal Board. His name was Zoran Stanic.

utterances.speaker: MS. PIDWELL
utterances.text: Sir --

utterances.speaker: MS. PIDWELL
utterances.text: Could I please have 65 ter 2662 on the screen?

utterances.speaker: MS. PIDWELL
utterances.text: Do you see that document before you, sir?

utterances.speaker: SIMO MISKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. PIDWELL
utterances.text: And the title is -- I think we've got the -- go to the next page on the English, please. The book of minutes of the Prijedor SDS Municipal Board meetings, archive book number 7, 1991 volume.

utterances.speaker: MS. PIDWELL
utterances.text: And if we just flick to page -- the first page in the B/C/S where it's handwritten; page 3 perhaps. The next page, please. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. PIDWELL
utterances.text: If you have a look at that, just -- do you recognise the handwriting, sir?

utterances.speaker: SIMO MISKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: This is the 23rd, is that right, 1991?

utterances.speaker: MS. PIDWELL
utterances.text: Yes. You can see that at the top.

utterances.speaker: SIMO MISKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That was before my time, before I came to the head of the party.

utterances.speaker: MS. PIDWELL
utterances.text: All right. Do you remember -- you said there were no minutes taken before you became president. Is my recollection correct?

utterances.speaker: SIMO MISKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I didn't find any, and this is why I insisted on it and I even replaced two of the secretaries. There were two secretaries, and I brought this Zoran Stanic who did the job professionally. As for this one, these minutes, I wasn't there at the time, so I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MS. PIDWELL
utterances.text: Let's go, for example, to a period of time when you were there which is further on.

utterances.speaker: SIMO MISKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, after the 11th of September.

utterances.speaker: MS. PIDWELL
utterances.text: Let's just take a look.

utterances.speaker: MS. PIDWELL
utterances.text: Perhaps if we go to page, in the B/C/S, headed 10 -- sorry. 01021655. And the English is 1 -- 00916443.

utterances.speaker: MS. PIDWELL
utterances.text: If we just take this as an example, sir, you will see this is a headed 31 January 1992. Do you see that?

utterances.speaker: SIMO MISKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: 1992, yes, yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. PIDWELL
utterances.text: Minutes of the SDS Municipal Board meeting with you presiding.

utterances.speaker: SIMO MISKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, yes, presiding, yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. PIDWELL
utterances.text: And there's an agenda with three items underneath it.

utterances.speaker: SIMO MISKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. PIDWELL
utterances.text: Agenda was unanimously adopted. Says Miskovic gave a briefing on the session of the Bosanska Krajina Assembly. Do you see that?

utterances.speaker: SIMO MISKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. Meeting of the Assembly of Bosanska Krajina, and the Serbian Assembly, and the Serbian Assembly of the B and H.

utterances.speaker: MS. PIDWELL
utterances.text: Does that mean that you had actually gone to an assembly session yourself?

utterances.speaker: SIMO MISKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't remember. I can see that it says here Bosanska Krajina and the Serbian Assembly of Bosnia and Herzegovina. I don't know the context. It says both, Serbian Krajina and the Serbian Assembly of the B and H. I don't know whether organisation was discussed or something. I cannot remember that now. But, yes, the information, you can see that it's there. It says assemblies, in the plural. The Bosnian Krajina and the Serbian Assembly of the B and H.

utterances.speaker: MS. PIDWELL
utterances.text: In your role as president of the SDS for Prijedor, did you attend, on occasion, assembly meetings of the Krajina?

utterances.speaker: SIMO MISKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. I did go from time to time, yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. PIDWELL
utterances.text: And would you then report back to your own -- to your own region on whatever was occurring in the assembly session that you attended?

utterances.speaker: SIMO MISKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Not the region but members of the Main Board. I informed them about everything, you know. When I was looking at the material I said that my principle was since the Municipal Board was comprised of members of the local board, I wanted everyone to be acquainted in the region about what's going on so that everybody would be informed of what is going on. That was my principle. Well, as for how much people actually reflect -- respected that request, I don't know. But, anyway, that was my principle, my approach to these matters.

utterances.speaker: MS. PIDWELL
utterances.text: Thank you. And if we go to the end of those minutes on that day, which is, in the English, five pages on to 00916447. And in the B/C/S, it's the page headed 01021662. So this looks like the end of the meeting, and you can see there at the -- the bottom it says: "Minutes drafted by ..." And can you work out who drafted those minutes?

utterances.speaker: SIMO MISKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It doesn't say here who drafted it. At least I don't see it. It's not there.

utterances.speaker: MS. PIDWELL
utterances.text: My apologies, sir.

utterances.speaker: MS. PIDWELL
utterances.text: I need the next page in the B/C/S.

utterances.speaker: SIMO MISKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Vinko. Vinko, the secretary.

utterances.speaker: MS. PIDWELL
utterances.text: Do you know that man?

utterances.speaker: SIMO MISKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. He was one of the secretaries of the Municipal Board.

utterances.speaker: MS. PIDWELL
utterances.text: What was his full name? Vinko ...

utterances.speaker: SIMO MISKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I've forgotten his last name. I might remember it later. And as for the other one, I have forgotten both his first and last name. He was an economist by profession. Kos.

utterances.speaker: MS. PIDWELL
utterances.text: Vinko Kos?

utterances.speaker: SIMO MISKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. PIDWELL
utterances.text: If we go back to the preceding page in the B/C/S only, please. Do you see there, sir, where it mentions that Simo Drljaca is appointed the head of the Committee for Internal Cooperation?

utterances.speaker: SIMO MISKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I do.

utterances.speaker: MS. PIDWELL
utterances.text: What was the Committee for Internal Cooperation?

utterances.speaker: SIMO MISKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The Committee for Internal Cooperation was a commission that was supposed to monitor the conduct and activities of members of the party. And then later, Simo will be proposed as chief of the MUP from this post here.

utterances.speaker: MS. PIDWELL
utterances.text: And he was -- was he a member of the SDS Municipal Board at this time?

utterances.speaker: SIMO MISKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. He was proposed by Milan Babic, who was a teacher and who was on good terms with him. Milan Babic was a member of the Municipal Board.

utterances.speaker: MS. PIDWELL
utterances.text: If we turn to the next page, please, in the English, which is the next meeting, just to give a further example.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: Ms. Pidwell, perhaps it is my own impatience, but it seems to me that, whereas it appears that you're meticulously laying out a path to take us somewhere, that is it necessary to stop at every street corner and every feature on the road? Could we rapidly get to where you are taking us? You just prefaced your question about to ask for another example, the last example which took us about ten minutes, I'm not sure how illuminating it was.

utterances.speaker: MS. PIDWELL
utterances.text: Well, Your Honour, if you will allow me to tender the book of the minutes of the Prijedor SDS at this juncture, I will simply do that and carry on. But if you -- I was laying the foundation to show that this corroborates his testimony that meetings were held every week, minutes were taken, he presided, and obviously we've got a document which show which shows what occurred at those meetings, agendas, minutes, decision made. If you are happy for me to tender it at this juncture, I will do so and move on to another issue.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: Before we rule on that, coming back to the exchange earlier with Mr. Krgovic's intervention about the relevance of these events back to 1991, and remembering well your explanation, would we need all those minute books to be incorporated into the body of evidence?

utterances.speaker: MS. PIDWELL
utterances.text: If my submission, yes, sir. And I wonder if the witness could take off his headphones while I provide my explanation.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: Yes. Mr. Miskovic, could you kindly remove your headphones. Yes, Ms. Pidwell.

utterances.speaker: MS. PIDWELL
utterances.text: Your Honours, it's the Prosecution's position that the takeover of Prijedor was meticulously organised from a high level down through the ranks of the SDS, through to the Municipal Board, down to the police and the army working in close co-operation together. The -- the organisation and the minutes which preceded the actual takeover in April are extremely relevant to the Prosecution proving, not only that the accused Zupljanin was involved in those events, but also that the accused Stanisic was involved in terms of the JCE principles and the involvement of the high-level members of the SDS.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: Could we hear the Defence on this issue.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: Your Honours, I find this particular -- this evidence is irrelevant for this case. And precisely this evidence from 1991, the Prosecution must be focussed on particular meeting where this plan was done or prepared. Not generally put the -- this kind of evidence. Look at this evidence shown this. So the Prosecution must be focussed on particular meeting when the plan was developed, for example. Allegedly.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: Which was essentially my question, Ms. Pidwell. Is it possible, is it practical to be more precise in terms of the portions of the minutes on which you are relying rather than just putting the whole -- I -- I don't know what volume of material this is we're talking about it. It may be that it is so relevantly small that it is insignificant. But just on the chance, and we're dealing with being burdened with a -- extra paper, is it possible for the Prosecution to be more precise in terms of what it's going to tender?

utterances.speaker: MS. PIDWELL
utterances.text: Your Honours, I was attempting to be precise and take you through particular meetings as examples of what was incorporated in the greater context, and then, at the end, to tender the entire book to show the consistency of these meetings with these examples and dispersed. I'm really in your hands as to how you would like me to do this.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: Ms. Pidwell, what we would invite you to do, what we would require you to do, is to bring the witness who is presently on the stand home to the various portions of the minutes which are relevant to what you are trying to prove, rather than tendering -- just putting the whole book of minutes in, or books of minutes in.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HARHOFF
utterances.text: Sir.

utterances.speaker: MS. PIDWELL
utterances.text: Can we have, please, page 00916397 - it's back - on the screen, please. Page 62 in e-court. And it's page 1002 -- sorry. 01021594 in the B/C/S. Page 91. Sorry, I need to start with the commencement of that session. So that would be 01021591 in the B/C/S.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: Ms. Pidwell, although we're about four minutes ahead of the usual time for rising, it seems that this might be a convenient point to take the break, since you're likely to send some time on this.

utterances.speaker: MS. PIDWELL
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: And I alert counsel that when we take the next break at 12.05, it will be a 35-minutes duration. We will be resuming at 12.40. We rise.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: I just wish to modify briefly what I said about the time for the next break. We will rise at 12.10 and resume at 12.40.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: Ms. Pidwell, I suppose this is an reason why you're taking us back to the meeting of the 11 of September, 1991?

utterances.speaker: MS. PIDWELL
utterances.text: There is, Your Honour. It is the day he was appointed as the SDS president and on his own evidence was the day that he was involved from -- as the party's president from then on. I will then take you to -- I have selected five additional entries, 11th of September, 27th of December, and then three entries in February from this book of minutes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. PIDWELL
utterances.text: So before the break, we were reviewing entries from the book of minutes from the Prijedor municipality, municipal organs of the Serbian Democratic Party. You will see on your screen the minutes of the 11th of September, 1991.

utterances.speaker: MS. PIDWELL
utterances.text: And if we go to the third page in the English, so headed 6399, and in the B/C/S, it's the page headed 1594. Sorry, the English should be 6399. 6399. 64. And the B/C/S should be headed 1594. That's it.

utterances.speaker: MS. PIDWELL
utterances.text: We see your name there, sir, under number 1, about halfway down the page, being proposed as a candidate for the post of president of the SDS. Do you see that? And --

utterances.speaker: SIMO MISKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, yes, I see it.

utterances.speaker: MS. PIDWELL
utterances.text: And at the bottom of the page we see the conclusions of the vote, with you receiving 121 votes and your opponent 13.

utterances.speaker: SIMO MISKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The second candidate, 13.

utterances.speaker: MS. PIDWELL
utterances.text: Is that a true reflection of the voting at the time, to your recollection?

utterances.speaker: SIMO MISKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. PIDWELL
utterances.text: I want to take you now to the minutes of the 27th of December.

utterances.speaker: MS. PIDWELL
utterances.text: Page 103 in e-court for the English, and page 144 in the B/C/S.

utterances.speaker: MS. PIDWELL
utterances.text: Do you recall attending the -- this meeting on the 27th of December in your role as president?

utterances.speaker: SIMO MISKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, yes, of course, as the president, I must have done, for sure. And I presided over the meeting too.

utterances.speaker: MS. PIDWELL
utterances.text: And we see there, after the agenda, under number 1, that you read out the instruction delivered to the Prijedor Municipal Board of the SDS by the Serbian Assembly. Do you see that?

utterances.speaker: SIMO MISKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. PIDWELL
utterances.text: What instruction is that referring to?

utterances.speaker: SIMO MISKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: From what I can see at the end, this is Variant B that was involved, and then it says: "Variant B." I assume that that's that.

utterances.speaker: MS. PIDWELL
utterances.text: From your perspective of the president of the Prijedor SDS, could you explain what Variant B -- what the instruction was that we know as Variant A and B?

utterances.speaker: SIMO MISKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, Variants A and B existed as instructions for the conduct of the SDS in two different situations. The first -- in the -- in municipality. The first situation was -- would be the one where the Serbs gained the majority in a general election. And the other when somebody else gained a majority. In Prijedor, those would be Muslims. So in Variant B applies to Prijedor. What does it imply, actually? It's about the Serbian People led by the Serbian Democratic Party as the movement for Bosnia who -- and the Serbian People should be protected from any unpleasant surprises that might again lead to the hardship of the Serbian People. In that context and from the instructions set out in Variant B, you can see that it concerns the preparation of the cadres of the representatives of the Serbian People to react in a case of any danger that might lead to the escalation of violence or confrontations and conflicts in that area. In such a situation, or in that situation, Variant II envisaged the establishment or authorities that would assume responsibility for preventing any confrontations. In that -- with that view, the shadow cabinet was formed that composed of Serbian members of the government and others who were not government members. The Territorial Defence functioned along the same principle as a military formation. The head of the Territorial Defence in Prijedor was Slobodan Kuruzovic. And the chief of the MUP was Simo Drljaca who was appointed at Babic's proposal. That was all on paper, as it were. That's how it was until -- for as long as there was a threat of confrontations in the territory of Prijedor.

utterances.speaker: MS. PIDWELL
utterances.text: From whom did you receive these instructions?

utterances.speaker: SIMO MISKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Received those at a meeting in Sarajevo -- or, rather, in Pale, a meeting that we attended, but I can't be sure of the exact location. All party presidents were present at the meeting, as well as deputies in the National Assembly. The paper was distributed, and we were asked to act accordingly and to convey the instructions to the Municipal Boards and inform them about the existence of the two variants.

utterances.speaker: MS. PIDWELL
utterances.text: Who presided over that meeting in Sarajevo?

utterances.speaker: SIMO MISKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The president of the party, Radovan Karadzic.

utterances.speaker: MS. PIDWELL
utterances.text: I want to take you now to the minutes of the meeting on the 7th of February.

utterances.speaker: MS. PIDWELL
utterances.text: And if we can have, please, page P113 in e-court in English.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] 7 January, or, rather, 7 January.

utterances.speaker: MS. PIDWELL
utterances.text: Just one moment.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can you take another look? I believe it is the 7th of January, 2002. That's, I believe, what you have in mind.

utterances.speaker: MS. PIDWELL
utterances.text: Well, if we are doing it chronologically, yes, sir. But I'd like to take you to the meeting on 7 February meeting. Which is on page P113 in English.

utterances.speaker: SIMO MISKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I apologise, I apologise.

utterances.speaker: MS. PIDWELL
utterances.text: And in the B/C/S, it's 161.

utterances.speaker: MS. PIDWELL
utterances.text: So we see here the minutes from the 7th of February with a note that every Thursday at 1700 a meeting of the SDS Prijedor Municipal Board is held. Do you see that?

utterances.speaker: SIMO MISKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, yes, yes. I have already told you, as far as I can remember. You can see that is what has been established, that we would be meeting once a week. And it is a Thursday, just as I told you it was, that there was a slot on Thursdays.

utterances.speaker: MS. PIDWELL
utterances.text: And can we go, please, to page 6452 in the English. And 1671 in the B/C/S.

utterances.speaker: MS. PIDWELL
utterances.text: I know it's difficult to read, sir, but there is a portion there which in the B/C/S - it may be on the preceding page - but it has got your name above it, Miskovic and it starts: "Since no specific accusations have been brought up ..." The portion I want to draw your attention to is where you say -- or it's recorded as you saying: "Our option is to create a Serbian state. There is also the constitution of the Autonomous Region of Krajina and we are waiting for the final solution. Block what we can, until the Serbian state is defined under any option. That is why it is demanded of all of us to as people do our best for the salvation of the Serbian People." Do you see that portion, sir, in the minutes?

utterances.speaker: SIMO MISKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I don't. I can't find it. I'm looking, but I can't find it. Where is that? Am I looking at the right page? Ah, now have I got it, our -- yes, "option." Our option is to create ... Where does it say that I'm the one who says this.

utterances.speaker: MS. PIDWELL
utterances.text: Sir, if you look at the top of the page --

utterances.speaker: SIMO MISKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't see it. I can't find it here. Aha, Miskovic here, okay.

utterances.speaker: MS. PIDWELL
utterances.text: Do you accept, sir, that's a --

utterances.speaker: SIMO MISKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I have got it now, yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. PIDWELL
utterances.text: Do you accept, sir, that that's a true record of what you said at that meeting?

utterances.speaker: SIMO MISKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Probably, yes. Well, I can't read everything. I would like to be able to see the context and the reason why I said what I did, why this was said in the first place. What was the context of the whole thing.

utterances.speaker: MS. PIDWELL
utterances.text: Sir, I want to take you now to the -- a meeting the next week on the 13th of February.

utterances.speaker: MS. PIDWELL
utterances.text: In the English --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Because it says here three options.

utterances.speaker: MS. PIDWELL
utterances.text: In the English, it's page 119 in e-court. And -- sorry. The B/C/S is page 170.

utterances.speaker: MS. PIDWELL
utterances.text: This is minutes of a meeting a week later, on the 13th of February. Once again, at 1715, chaired by you?

utterances.speaker: SIMO MISKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. PIDWELL
utterances.text: Do you see that?

utterances.speaker: SIMO MISKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. I chaired every one of them. There's no dispute about that.

utterances.speaker: MS. PIDWELL
utterances.text: Can we turn now to the next page, please, on each. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. PIDWELL
utterances.text: I just want to draw your attention to item number 3, if you can make it out.

utterances.speaker: SIMO MISKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Among --

utterances.speaker: MS. PIDWELL
utterances.text: Sorry, in the B/C/S, it's the next page. Just after halfway down the page, sir, there's an item, number 3 which is headed any other business. Do you see that?

utterances.speaker: SIMO MISKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Any other business, yes, yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. PIDWELL
utterances.text: And it states there that: "Meeting of the Main Board in Sarajevo is scheduled for tomorrow and the local board members and the vice-president are going." Do you see that?

utterances.speaker: SIMO MISKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I don't. Under 3, I can see any other reasons meeting of the Main Board in Sarajevo is scheduled for tomorrow and as standing for -- deputies are going and the vice-president. And the vice-president. I don't know who the vice-president is. I don't know who went.

utterances.speaker: MS. PIDWELL
utterances.text: Sir, do you recall a meeting which took place on the 14th of February at the Holiday Inn in Sarajevo?

utterances.speaker: SIMO MISKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I do. That was in 1991, or thereabouts, I think. I think it was in 1991. Or maybe 1992, at the beginning. Or in 1991, I -- I believe. When communication was still normal, when relations were still normal.

utterances.speaker: MS. PIDWELL
utterances.text: I have one more entry to go, but just -- I'm going to move to another document and I'll come back to the last entry in this series of minutes. If I could have 65 ter 01725. It's P1358-17.

utterances.speaker: MS. PIDWELL
utterances.text: Sorry, that's the wrong document. It's P1353 -- sorry. I said 58. 1353.17.

utterances.speaker: MR. CVIJETIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Just the table number, please, or the tab number.

utterances.speaker: MS. PIDWELL
utterances.text: Tab 13A. I apologise, Your Honours. This is an ERN range. It's a series of receipts and trying to identify the particular one which relates to the witness.

utterances.speaker: MS. PIDWELL
utterances.text: I'm told that the quickest way is to put it in Sanction, if Your Honours are happy with that.

utterances.speaker: MS. PIDWELL
utterances.text: Sir, do you see this -- this document in front of you, and are you able to read it?

utterances.speaker: SIMO MISKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Not really.

utterances.speaker: MS. PIDWELL
utterances.text: Would you expect that it's a receipt from the Holiday Inn hotel in Sarajevo in your name?

utterances.speaker: SIMO MISKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I can see it is. But I can't see my name. But that doesn't mean I wasn't there. I was. But I can't see it in here. I don't see my own name on this receipt, and I can't see the date well either. But I did spend the night at Holiday Inn. I was there. Now I can see it in this receipt. I can see Miskovic, 15 February, but I don't know what year. Well, I -- I certainly was at Holiday Inn. I attended a meeting of the Main Board. I also overnighted at the hotel. There's no dispute about that at all.

utterances.speaker: MS. PIDWELL
utterances.text: Let's move on then. Back to the book of minutes, please, and we'll go to the last entry that I want to deal with, which was on the 17th of February.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HARHOFF
utterances.text: Mr. Miskovic, while we're waiting for the next document to come up, I think there's still an outstanding issue of exactly which year you were at Holiday Inn. Was it from the 14th to the 15th February, 1991, or 1992?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I can't remember. I only remember that the relations were still normal, which means that all parties and party representatives communicated, and I know that after having spent that night in Holiday Inn, in the morning, I met Mirza Mujadzic, an SDA member. He had come in a Golf II car of green colour. I asked him where he got the car from, and he says, Alija gave me, and then we joked and I told him, Well, we don't have the money to buy cars, why don't you get us the money to buy a car for us. Then relations were still normal. We still joked together. We joked around, and things were quite differently then. And I'm still not sure about the date. And I'm not disputing the fact that there was a meeting, that we overnighted at the hotel. There is nothing in dispute about that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HARHOFF
utterances.text: Of course, it makes a great difference whether this meeting took place in 1991 or 1992. But I give the floor back to Ms. Pidwell.

utterances.speaker: MS. PIDWELL
utterances.text: Sir, when you attended this meeting, was it in your capacity as president of the SDS Prijedor?

utterances.speaker: SIMO MISKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, as the president of the Municipal Board of the SDS in Prijedor, and members of the National Assembly from Prijedor also attended. Srdjo Srdic and Timara Teser [phoen].

utterances.speaker: MS. PIDWELL
utterances.text: And we know that you were elected on the 11th of September, 1991; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: SIMO MISKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. PIDWELL
utterances.text: So by natural common sense, if you attended this meeting after your election as president, it would have been in the year 1992; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: SIMO MISKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I said that that either was in late 1990 or early 1991. But I don't know exactly when it was. All I know is that the relations were normal and that we were still able to crack jokes together. And that's the only time that I spent a night at Holiday Inn. That was the only occasion for me.

utterances.speaker: MS. PIDWELL
utterances.text: Sir, you said late 1990 or early 1991. In late 1990 and early 1991 --

utterances.speaker: SIMO MISKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, no, late 1991. I misspoke, I'm sorry. 1991 or early 1992. I misspoke, I apologise.

utterances.speaker: MS. PIDWELL
utterances.text: Thank you. Let's go back to the book of minutes and this may clarify things once and for all.

utterances.speaker: MS. PIDWELL
utterances.text: Let's go to the 17th of February. English, it's page 122; and the B/C/S, in e-court, it's 174.

utterances.speaker: MS. PIDWELL
utterances.text: Sir, the first item on the agenda we see is the briefing on the meeting of the Main Board and the Serbian Assembly of BH. And then it reads: "After adopting the agenda (28 items) Simo Miskovic, president, ... gave a briefing on the meeting held in Sarajevo." Do you see that?

utterances.speaker: SIMO MISKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I do. Yes, that's all right. You see that was an assembly meeting. I thought it was a Main Board meeting, but it was an assembly meeting, as can you see.

utterances.speaker: MS. PIDWELL
utterances.text: And --

utterances.speaker: SIMO MISKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Of course, I'm talking about party meetings.

utterances.speaker: MS. PIDWELL
utterances.text: And there's a report there, your report, that Dr. Karadzic was the main speaker; do you see that?

utterances.speaker: SIMO MISKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, yes. As the party president.

utterances.speaker: MS. PIDWELL
utterances.text: And you report that there's been an act of cessation of the BH -- do you see that?

utterances.speaker: SIMO MISKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Cessation of Bosnia-Herzegovina on the part of the SDA. And in that sense, we were forced to create national or ethnic communities. That's how I read it. National communities on -- on problems.

utterances.speaker: MS. PIDWELL
utterances.text: So you're --

utterances.speaker: SIMO MISKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know. I can't ... The position of the European community was stated. The European community will not interfere with internal solutions of the -- that's all in the minutes, the discussion on the Serbian, so on and so forth.

utterances.speaker: MS. PIDWELL
utterances.text: Yes, sir. Do you recall that you're relaying, or are you relaying what -- what was -- what occurred at the meeting in Sarajevo back to your Municipal Board?

utterances.speaker: SIMO MISKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That was a rule I followed, and I did it at that time. I always informed the Municipal Board and since Municipal Boards were also composed of presidents of local boards, I asked them to inform members at local levels. That was the principle of work I always followed.

utterances.speaker: MS. PIDWELL
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. PIDWELL
utterances.text: Now we can move -- I think the English is the same. But if we could move, please, to the next page in the B/C/S. It's about halfway -- the second paragraph in the B/C/S, so halfway down the page.

utterances.speaker: MS. PIDWELL
utterances.text: You see it's a continuation of your report on this meeting. And it stated there that you reported: "That Serbs shall not participate in any way in the referendum conducted by the SDA." Do you see that?

utterances.speaker: SIMO MISKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can't find that, but I know that that happened. His participation in -- or in the aspect in the referendum, which has been conducted by the SDA ... in view of that.

utterances.speaker: MS. PIDWELL
utterances.text: What referendum --

utterances.speaker: SIMO MISKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: To activate the second page of the position stated by the SDS BH Main Board. Or, rather, to activate the territory and the population, Serbs, in brackets, by activists. It -- I don't know. I can't read it. I can't --

utterances.speaker: MS. PIDWELL
utterances.text: I appreciate it's difficult, sir. But do you -- my question is: Was there a direction for the Serbs not to participant in the referendum which was being conducted by the SDA at that time?

utterances.speaker: SIMO MISKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, of course, it was. Because the goal was to secede Bosnia and Herzegovina from Yugoslavia and that's the context of the entire story, and, in that regard, the Serbs thought that it would be threatened, and for that reason they refused to participate in the referendum because the decision on the referendum was worded in that sense, and it was made by the rump assembly of Bosnia and Herzegovina and they excluded representatives of the Serbian People from any of that.

utterances.speaker: MS. PIDWELL
utterances.text: And was there also a direction to activate the second stage of the Variant A and B instruction?

utterances.speaker: SIMO MISKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know if it was at that point in time, but you can see from the document that it was activated at the point in time when there was a threat that there could be a confrontation, a conflict, escalation of the conflict. In that case the Variant B would go into effect. And as you could see, following the entire course of the events, and after the takeover of power, that there were no confrontations. It -- they didn't happen before or after that until the incidents that led to the escalation of events. I'm talking about the genesis of events, actually, until this formation.

utterances.speaker: MS. PIDWELL
utterances.text: The minutes that we're looking at, sir, say -- or report that it's necessary to activate the second stage of the position stated by the SDS, BH Main Board, namely, Variant A and B at this time. Do you accept that at this meeting --

utterances.speaker: SIMO MISKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Variant B, yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. PIDWELL
utterances.text: Do you accept that at this board meeting the conclusion was made to activate the second stage of Variant B, by the Prijedor Municipal Board?

utterances.speaker: SIMO MISKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: You mean was that a decision by the Municipal Board at the time that work should be done on the activation of Variant B? Is that what you meant? If that's what you meant, then, yes. Preparations.

utterances.speaker: MS. PIDWELL
utterances.text: And if we turn to the next page in the English. And in the B/C/S it is the page headed 160, so two pages on.

utterances.speaker: MS. PIDWELL
utterances.text: There's some discussion there headed by Srdjo Srdic about the Serbian coat of arms anthem and flag which was unanimously adopted by the Municipal Board. Can you see that in your version?

utterances.speaker: SIMO MISKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. I can see that it says Srdjo Srdic here. An important argument about our transformation is our plebescite which we implemented, yes. The creation ... there was a ... directives emigration, migrations and moving in and the substitution of territories is inevitable. I -- I can't read this.

utterances.speaker: MS. PIDWELL
utterances.text: Just pause, please, sir.

utterances.speaker: MS. PIDWELL
utterances.text: Your Honours, I've come to the conclusion of the extracts from this book of minutes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HARHOFF
utterances.text: But before we leave the page here, Mr. Miskovic, do you recall what was meant by the substitution of territories? If you read again the last lines of what you just read out from the minutes, do you know --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Srdjo Srdic was a deputy from the Prijedor municipality. Most probably, with a reserve here. Most probably this was something that was discussed at the Serbian Assembly of Bosnia and Herzegovina in which he took part as a deputy and that he is then informing the Municipal Board about that in this context. I don't know if, at the level of the B and H, there was a conversation among the party representatives, I don't know. He was a deputy, so this is probably something relating to that, something in which he took part.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HARHOFF
utterances.text: I understand that, sir. My question to you is: If you recall, what exactly Mr. Srdic meant when he referred to the substitution of territories.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Territories. From this perspective I can only assume that this was a question of exchanging territories with the concentration of one population with those -- with the concentration of the other population. I mean, I am just assuming that. I cannot recall that, really, on the basis of this.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HARHOFF
utterances.text: But, sir, you were there. You took part in the discussions about this. You must have had some sort of an idea what was going to happen and, actually, in light of what later on did happen.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] What happened later are the consequences. As I said, most probably, this conversation might reflect something that possibly was a conversation at the top of the leadership in the parliament between party members. I don't know that, and I assume that Srdjo Srdic was reporting this at our meeting of the Municipal Board because at our meetings, this item was never something that was on the agenda at the Main Board in which -- in the work of which I participated. I know that. I don't know whether this took place some -- at the parliament or the Serbian Assembly that had split off so I assume that Srdjo Srdic is informing about this as a parliament reporting back the information that has to do with these proposals relating to the exchange of territories. Everything else that I could say would be incorrect.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HARHOFF
utterances.text: When you -- when you say that there was supposed to be an exchange of territories, just how was that supposed to -- to take place? Do you mean that -- that Muslims would give up territories in one place in return for getting territories in another place? Is that what you mean by the expression "exchange of territories"?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] When I said this earlier, this is precisely what I meant, that this was something discussed and agreed at some other level. This was not put on the agenda on the party and it was never discussed in the Main Board or the Municipal Board. This is an idea that Srdjo Srdic, as a people's deputy, probably discussed at the Serbian Assembly where suggestions may have been put forward on one and the other side perhaps. I don't know about that. He was relaying back information here about that, but I don't know anything specifically about that report.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HARHOFF
utterances.text: And just to clarify before I give the floor back to Ms. Pidwell, you are saying that this issue of exchange of territories was never discussed at the Municipal Board in Prijedor?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, yes. Yes, yes. The Main Board where I participated, as far as I know, never discussed that. It was never on the agenda.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: Your Honours, just one small clarification for the transcript because it is not properly recorded what the witness say. It's page 42, line 7, witness said when I said this is precisely what I said and it was discussed on the republic level, and after that, this is the ... .

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HARHOFF
utterances.text: I'm not sure what to make of your observation, Mr. Krgovic. I suppose that what we --

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: Just maybe please can repeat the answer.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HARHOFF
utterances.text: Please -- Right. Mr. Miskovic, following the intervention by Mr. Krgovic, I would kindly ask you to repeat your last answer, if you could.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The party meetings, meetings of the party of the Municipal Board and the Main Board where I was present, the topic of exchange of territories was never on the agenda.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HARHOFF
utterances.text: Thank you, sir. Back to Ms. Pidwell.

utterances.speaker: MS. PIDWELL
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour. Your Honours, I have, as you see, extracted five or six -- six, I think, days of the minutes from this book. My submission is that the whole book should be tendered to provide the overall context and continuity of the meetings that were held by the board. It's one document, if we're talking about a hard copy document and the relevant portions have obviously been highlighted in the transcript. But in my submission, it's more appropriate for the entire document to be exhibited because there may be other portions of it that become relevant at a later date.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HARHOFF
utterances.text: Thank you, Ms. Pidwell. I think you set out to identify the portions of this book of minutes in which the planning of the takeover of Prijedor was discussed or mentioned, and having now seen the five or six passages to which you have referred, I'm not sure that this refers directly to the takeover of Prijedor. So my question to you is: Are there other passages in the book of minutes which do address, or mention, or refer to the possible discussions in the SDS Municipal Board in Prijedor in 1992 to take over the municipality of Prijedor?

utterances.speaker: MS. PIDWELL
utterances.text: Your Honour, it's not as simple as identifying one or two conversations in this book of minutes about the takeover. The takeover was -- perhaps if the witness could take off his headphones, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HARHOFF
utterances.text: Mr. Miskovic, would you be good enough to take off your headphones, just for a second.

utterances.speaker: MS. PIDWELL
utterances.text: It's the Prosecution's position that the -- the takeover was planned meticulously at several different levels. What was happening was instructions were coming from above as -- and there are some examples in the book of minutes of that. Instructions being received, the Variant A and B, which he then reads out to the board and then is implemented in various ways which are not directly recorded as we are now implementing X, Y and Z of Variant B but within the minutes can you see examples of it actually occurring. So it's the Prosecution's position that by reading the entire set of minutes, you get a sense of what was happening in the area at the time and the planning that was going on, the discussions that were taking place, the shadow government that was being set out and was waiting in the wings, and this all happened -- and what the witness will say was an extremely successful bloodless takeover because the -- of the planning that was involved. Now, we have this book of minutes. It is contemporaneous with the meetings that were taking place. He was authenticated it to the point where he says, yes, those meetings took place with even the detail being the time and the place, and so forth, and it's my submission that this would assist Your Honours greatly when considering the background to what is -- what took place in Prijedor.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: Ms. Pidwell, the witness may -- may -- You may replace your headphones. The Chamber, by a majority, agrees that the book -- that -- that the minutes, as a whole, could and should be admitted. However, as a purely practical matter, we are concerned, less immediately than down the road, when we must assess the evidence as to how to -- and I'm trying to avoid the use of the word highlight because it has such a variety of meanings. We can highlight what it is we ought to be directed to beyond what you have already done by the viva voce evidence you have led from the witness.
